title: Friction Kiln: customer scrapbook + quick probes
content:
TL;DR:
A compact, messy scrapbook of customer quotes and 6 rapid probes we can run in the next sprint. Focus: runtime behavior (KV cache/prefixing), sudden tail latency spikes for bursty workloads, and small UX/controls customers want to avoid costly backfills. These are low-effort changes with measurable impact (error-rate down, tail latency down, clear CSAT lift).

Why this doc:
- We keep getting repeat asks framed differently. This is a working list for quick engineering spikes and CS playbooks.
- Aim to ship small, observable fixes that unblock paying customers without heavy infra work.

Raw customer snippets (unedited):
- "We see random 95th spikes only when multiple short requests come in — it feels like cache cold starts firing simultaneously." (Fintech customer)
- "Our embedding costs jumped after the model switch; can we pin a cheaper quantized variant for a route?" (SaaS search vendor)
- "Rate limits are fine, but the burst rejections cause our UX to show 502s. A soft-queue or hint would be perfect." (marketplace)
- "When the model falls back the outputs look very different — customers prefer 'degraded but consistent' over unexpected hallucinations." (enterprise legal)

Synthesis / persistent themes:
1) KV/prefix cache cold-paths: short request bursts (chat-like) often incur full kv rebuilds; customers see tail latency spikes.
2) Controlled fallbacks: when we route to cheaper/compatible model variants, output drift causes user confusion. They want a configurable fallback policy (graceful noise reduction).
3) Burst handling UX: customers prefer queued/queued-with-progress vs immediate 429/502.
4) Cost-bound routing: customers want route-level preferences (e.g., prefer quantized-ggml-compatible variants when cost thresholds hit).
5) Observability: teams need token-level and model-variant traces surfaced as a single row in Console for quick blame.

Prioritized quick probes (ranked by expected impact / engineering hours):
A. kv-prefetch-toggle (2–3 engineer-days) — Introduce a per-route boolean to enable aggressive KV prefetch for short-sequence traffic.
   - Goal: reduce 95th latency for bursts by 20–40% for impacted customers.
   - Metrics: 95th latency pre/post, number of KV-miss rebuilds per minute.
   - Rollout: beta enable for 3 pilot accounts.

B. fallback-consistency-mode (3–5 engineer-days) — Add a 'consistency' fallback policy that, when falling back, uses constrained decoding/safer temperature and prefix constraints to keep outputs aligned.
   - Goal: reduce customer complaints about unexpected output drift.
   - Metrics: qualitative CS voice counts, automated similarity score between primary and fallback outputs.

C. burst-soft-queue (4 engineer-days + 1 SRE day) — lightweight soft-queue that returns immediate 202 + progress token instead of 502/429 when a brief capacity constraint is hit.
   - Goal: UX improvement for spikey workloads.
   - Metrics: drop in 502/429 for pilot routes, success rate of queued requests.

D. per-route-quant-preference (2 engineer-days) — route config to prefer quantized compatible model variants under cost thresholds; not strict fallback, just preference.
   - Goal: reduce token cost by up to 15% for eligible routes without severe latency impact.

E. dev-console-blame-row (3 engineer-days) — a single Console row that shows per-request: model-variant, route-config, token-count, kv-cache-hit, and latency.
   - Goal: shorten troubleshooting time; better CS->Eng handoffs.

F. pragmatic-kv-ttl (1–2 engineer-days) — configurable per-route KV TTL to keep prefix entries live for aggressive micro-sessions.
   - Goal: reduce cache churn for short repeated users.

Experiment design notes (lightweight):
- A/B groups: pick 10 pilot customer routes (mix of chat and short-reqs). For each probe, run 50/50 split for 1 week.
- Success thresholds: 95th latency down by 20% OR 502/429 down by 50% OR positive CSAT delta > +0.1 in pilot surveys.
- Rollback criteria: error rate increase > 1.5x baseline OR cost per token increase > 10% without latency improvement.

Quick implementation caveats / gotchas:
- kv-prefetch needs careful memory budgeting — SREs flagged potential OOMs for lower-memory nodes. (Slack: #sre-runtime thread ts: 1696213424)
- fallback-consistency similarity metric needs an embedding-based comparison; pick a compact embed (64–128d) to keep compute low.
- burst-soft-queue must integrate with existing rate-limiter and token billing paths to avoid double-billing.

Low-effort CS playbook (for now):
- When customers file: collect three samples (primary, fallback, diff) and tag with route-id + timestamp.
- Offer the per-route kv-ttl toggle as a manual pilot for top 5 affected accounts.
- Provide a canned explanation of fallback-consistency-mode as a short-term mitigation: "We can reduce output drift by constraining fallback sampling — outputs will be lower-variance and more predictable."

Open questions (to triage with Eng & Product):
- How much memory headroom do we realistically have for aggressive prefetch across Dedicated clusters? (Ask infra capacity team for numbers by GPU type)
- Can we compute a cheap similarity metric in-flight or should we sample 1/100 requests for post-hoc analysis?
- Legal/compliance: any concerns with queuing or delayed responses for regulated customers?

Immediate next steps (this sprint):
1) Triage with SRE on kv-prefetch memory impact (owner: Ravi) — due 2028-10-07.
2) Small design doc for fallback-consistency-mode (owner: Liam) — draft by 2028-10-06.
3) Wireframe Console blame-row in Figma and sync with DX (owner: Maya) — review 2028-10-09.
4) CS outreach: propose 3 pilot customers for kv-ttl and soft-queue testing (owner: Aisha) — outreach by 2028-10-06.

Notes to self: this is intentionally messy — keep it short and action-oriented when we send to Eng. Capture one sample trace per customer next week and attach to INF-4123.
